name: Clay Playful
tagline: Soft enough to squish, clear enough for a six-year-old.
description: A light-first system for children's products and the grown-ups around them. Things you can press or pick up are made of clay: thick rounded shapes in coral, mint, sky, and butter with an inner highlight and a pressed bottom edge that squashes when tapped. Everything else stays flat on cream. Rounded Fredoka headlines, Nunito for reading, big targets, and few words per screen.
useCases: consumer apps that want warmth without noise

fonts.role: display headlines, numbers, and button labels

palette.role: coral: the primary action fill; one per screen
coral as text: links and the active tab label
clay fill: correct answers, done, phonics category
clay fill: stars, streaks, word games category
text and icons on every clay fill, in both modes
light wash inside clay fills (pills, picture wells) so on-clay ink stays readable in both modes
errors and wrong answers, always with words
inner top highlight in the clay shadows
inner bottom edge and drop in the clay shadows

do: Give the clay shadow only to things you can press, pick up, or that float above the page: buttons, answer tiles, cards that open, toggle knobs, the toast
Squash clay on press: drop to the pressed shadow and move 2px down
Put on-clay ink on every pastel and coral fill, in both modes
Make tap targets at least 56px tall on child-facing screens
Say what happened in words next to every color signal: right, try again, done
dont: Do not put the clay shadow on panels, text blocks, or the page frame
Do not place icons inside pastel circles as decoration
Do not use pastels as text colors
Do not use more than one coral button on a screen
Do not use punishing language for wrong answers

components.name: Button
components.notes: Clay pills 56px tall. Primary is coral; secondary is surface clay; ghost is a coral text link. Pressing swaps to the pressed shadow and nudges 2px down with a squish ease.

components.name: Input
components.notes: Flat surface field with an inset well shadow, 20px radius, label above. Focus shows a 3px coral ring; error adds a danger border and a kind message.

components.name: Select
components.notes: Same well as the input with a rounded chevron; reading levels and ages.

components.name: Checkbox and toggle
components.notes: Rounded 8px checkbox that fills mint with a check. Switch is a well track with a clay knob that slides and turns the track mint.

components.name: Badge
components.notes: Flat pastel pills with on-clay text for categories and levels; a butter star count; a danger outline for an overdue lesson.

components.name: Card
components.notes: A lesson card made of clay: category pill, title, a drawn word picture, minutes and stars, and a coral start button.

components.name: Navbar
components.notes: Flat cream bar with the wordmark, child avatar initial, star count, and a grown-ups link. On phones it becomes a bottom tab bar of four clay tabs.

components.name: Modal and sheet
components.notes: Rounded 40px surface sheet with a grab handle, a short question for the child, and two big clay answers.

components.name: Table
components.notes: Grown-ups view of the week: day, lessons, minutes read, new words, with a mint dot for days done. Flat, no clay.

components.name: Bento grid
components.notes: Child home tiles: a flat butter streak tile with the week as day dots, today's lesson as a sky clay link, words learned, a sticker shelf, and a flat reading-time bar chart.

components.name: Empty state
components.notes: A drawn sleeping pebble, "No stickers yet", one line, one coral action.

components.name: Toast
components.notes: Mint clay pill at the top center: "Great reading!" with the star earned; shown for 3 seconds and announced politely.
